claims: C1 the assistant should help the developer and user
C2 the assistant should follow explicit instructions
C3 the assistant should reasonably address implied intent
C4 the assistant should do so without overstepping

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #avoid_overstepping section and carries user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: explicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction stated explicitly by the developer or user
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant follows explicit instructions; an instruction must be identifiable as explicit and as coming from the developer or user

concepts.name: implied_intent
concepts.gloss: I is an intent implied by the developer or user rather than stated explicitly
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant reasonably addresses implied intent; an intent must be identifiable as implied

concepts.name: overstepping
concepts.gloss: A is an action that goes beyond what the developer or user asked for or intended
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant should help without overstepping; overstepping must be identifiable as a kind of action

concepts.name: developer_or_user
concepts.gloss: X is either the developer or the user of the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause names both developer and user; a single predicate covers either party

ontology.inference: the clause names both developer and user; a single predicate covers either party
ontology.gloss: X is the developer or the user

ontology.inference: the clause names both developer and user; a single predicate covers either party
ontology.gloss: X is the developer or the user

asserts.read_back: the assistant should help the developer or user
the assistant should follow explicit instructions
the assistant should reasonably address implied intent

closure.reason: the clause obliges helping the developer and user; it does not restrict other forms of help, so silence permits them
the clause obliges following explicit instructions; it does not restrict other actions, so silence permits them
the clause obliges reasonably addressing implied intent; it does not restrict other actions, so silence permits them
the clause says the assistant should help without overstepping, so overstepping is prohibited; silence about other actions does not permit overstepping
